research_question: What natural mechanism lets a probably young neutron star reach an approximately 44.27-minute spin while retaining broadband coherent radio, intermittent X-rays, mode switching and sub-second radio structure?

current_survivor.label: FALLBACK_DISC_BRAKING_PLUS_MAGNETAR_LIKE_TWIST_DRIVEN_PAIR_CASCADES
current_survivor.evolution_layer: Fallback-disc interaction is a favored route to the ultralong spin if the SNR association is physical.
current_survivor.clock_layer: Rotation supplies the stable approximately 2656-s phase reference.
current_survivor.energy_plasma_layer: Magnetic free energy and local twists are a plausible source of accelerating voltage and intermittent pair plasma beyond ordinary pulsar deathline conditions.
current_survivor.radio_layer: Charge-starved pair discharges can plausibly support broadband coherent radio and dwarf-pulse-like sub-second events.
current_survivor.xray_layer: Twist dissipation and particle return currents can plausibly contribute variable X-ray/UV emission without requiring radio and X-rays to be co-spatial.
